Fix: Open till always opened the first location. The button carried no location at all, so the till fell back to whichever came first in the list. It now opens the location whose page you pressed it on. The Open till button on the locations list stays general, and a till opened without a location still starts on the first one.

1.92.2

Fix: trying to push a service to a sale location complained about the quantity. The push picker listed services even though a service can never be pushed, and its quantity field was capped at its workshop stock - zero - so the only answer you could ever get was "Enter a quantity", which was not the problem at all.

Services no longer appear as pushable rows. They are still named under the search results, with a note that they belong under Services offered here - so searching for one leads you to the right place instead of nowhere.

The same trap applied to any product with nothing at the workshop: it now says nothing at the workshop in place of a quantity box it could never accept a number in.

1.92.1

Fix: a product that already had stock at a sale location, then became a service, was stuck there. The till still counted those units and sold them as ordinary stock, and Pull back refused to touch them - so they could neither be sold correctly nor brought home.

Units left at a location from before an item became a service are now shown in that location's stock table, marked now a service - pull back, with the Pull back button working. The till no longer offers them: a service is sold from the location's service menu, not from a leftover quantity.

A service may not gain stock, but stock it already has can always leave. That is the rule the first release got wrong by refusing every movement - which also, quietly, would have lost the units on the way home from a location. A service that still holds stock now shows how much on its own page and offers Write off remaining and Set qty to clear it; both disappear once it is at zero, and Receive is never offered.

1.92.0

Products that are really services - sold, but never in stock. Tick A service - never in stock on any product: a workshop, a repair, engraving, a delivery fee. It can be sold as often as you like and never runs out. Pulling from the shop marks anything WooCommerce calls a virtual product as a service automatically.

Each sale location has its own service menu. A service is sold at a stall only after it has been added there, so the seaside stall need not offer what the Christmas market does. The location page gained a Services offered here card to add and remove them; at the till they appear alongside the stock, marked SERVICE instead of showing a quantity, and never greyed out as sold out.

A service is left out of everything that counts stock, rather than sitting at zero everywhere: no stock figure or Receive / Log use / Scrap / Set quantity on its page, no low-stock warning, no line in the stock valuation, and no stock level pushed to the shop. Its page shows where it is offered in place of how much is where.

Elsewhere: an order line for a service carries its price, VAT and what the partner owes, but moves no goods. A consignment note refuses one - you cannot leave a workshop on a partner's shelf; bill it on an order instead. Refunding a service at the till returns the money and puts nothing back on a shelf. Each location's service menu is treated as part of the location, like its name, so clearing test data before go-live keeps it.

1.91.0

The Produce list is now its own card, below the search box instead of inside it. Choosing what to make is the main act of that screen, so the list gets its own space rather than hanging off a form field.

Paged at 25. Long catalogues no longer render as one endless column - Previous / Next below the list, with the page number and the total. Turning a page needs no connection and no reloading; searching always returns you to page 1, so you are never left on page 3 of a list that just shrank.

Products with a recipe are listed first, alphabetically, with the recipe-less ones after them. They are still there - they can be produced, they just consume nothing - but they no longer sit between the products you actually make.

1.90.0

The Produce page now lists what you can make instead of waiting to be searched. Opening it shows every product you can produce, in one scrolling list; the box above narrows that list as you type rather than being the only way to see anything. Products with no recipe are listed too - they can still be produced, they just consume nothing - and are marked so you can tell at a glance.

The same fix on the recipe screen: pressing Add under Components now shows what there is to add straight away, and typing narrows it. The product itself is never offered, so a recipe cannot be made to contain its own output.

Narrowing either list is instant and needs no connection - the list is fetched once when the screen opens and filtered in the browser. On a catalogue large enough to reach the server's ceiling it goes back to the server instead, so a search can never quietly miss items that were not loaded.

Faster item lists. Shaping a list of items used to look up each one's recipe separately - one database query per row, so a 200-item list meant 200 extra queries. All recipes are now read once per request, which speeds up every list, report and picker in the app.

1.89.0

Log a use of a material that did not go through a recipe. A material page now has a Log use button beside Receive and Scrap - for the wax that went into a repair, the ribbon used on a sample, the batch spent on a workshop demo. You enter how much was used, the date it happened (so you can write up yesterday's work today) and what it was used for. It is recorded as the same kind of movement a production run makes when it consumes a component, so the history reads exactly as a recipe use does. Because the entry belongs to no document, it can be corrected in place with the pencil, or undone in correction mode, like any other hand-typed entry. Scrap is still the right button for stock that was lost rather than used.

1.88.5

Fix: giving a label a background colour made its QR code unreadable. On the darker colours the label's text switches to white for contrast - and the QR code was following it, so it was drawn white on its own white tile and effectively disappeared. The QR is now always black on white whatever colour the label is, while the name and SKU keep flipping for contrast as before. The white is painted inside the code itself (including its quiet border), so a label stays scannable when printed or when the SVG is downloaded and dropped onto someone else's sheet.

1.88.4

Materials now have their own category shortcuts in the sidebar, opening under Materials exactly as the product ones open under Products. Each list shows only its own categories and takes you to the matching filtered list, and the two open and close independently - so you can keep your materials expanded without the products list expanding too.

Fix: opening a material highlighted "Products" in the sidebar. Any item page lit up Products regardless of what the item was. A material - and its edit form and recipe - now correctly highlights Materials.

1.88.3

Fix: a calculated cost no longer freezes the moment you edit the item. Opening an item and saving it used to write whatever cost was on screen into the item - so a cost that had been working itself out (from a recipe, or from what your purchases cost) quietly became a fixed number and stopped updating. It now stays calculated unless you say otherwise.

You choose, per item: calculated or typed by hand. Where a cost can be worked out, the edit form shows the figure, says where it comes from - from recipe or from your purchases - and notes what keeps it up to date. Tick Enter the unit cost manually and the cost boxes appear and your number sticks; leave it unticked and the figure keeps tracking. Materials get this choice now too, not just items with a recipe. Margins on the form are measured against whichever figure is actually in effect.

1.88.2

Fix: an item's SKU can now actually be changed. The field was editable and saving said "Item saved", but the new SKU was quietly thrown away on the way to the database - so a typo in a SKU was permanent. It now saves. If another item already uses the SKU you type, the save is refused and tells you which item has it, rather than failing silently.

A warning where it matters: change the SKU of an existing item and the form points out that any QR label already printed for it carries the old code and will stop opening it - print a fresh label. The note appears only once you actually change the SKU. SKU changes are also recorded in the activity log, showing the old and new code.

1.88.1

Fix: bought materials showed no cost, and counted as free in recipes. If you never typed a price on a material, the list showed a dash - even though the app had already worked out what it cost from your purchase history. Worse, anything made from that material was costed as if the material were free, quietly understating every product's cost and overstating its margin. Materials now fall back to what your purchases say they cost, shown with the calculated tag, and recipes use that figure. A price you type still wins, a typed zero is still respected as a real answer, and a material with genuinely no purchase history still shows a dash.

1.88.0

Backfill stock on the day it actually arrived. Receiving or scrapping stock now has a Date field, so entering last week's delivery records it against last week - not today. It defaults to today, refuses future dates, and you can correct it later by editing the entry. Backdated deliveries slot into the material's price history in the right place.

Materials and products now have their own categories. They were sharing one list, so a jar size showed up when categorising a gift set. Each side now has its own set, and the picker on an item offers only the ones that fit what the item is - switching an item between product and material switches the list with it.

  • Your existing categories become product categories. Any used only by materials move to the material list automatically, and one used by both is copied to both sides so nothing loses its category. The same name can now exist on both sides.
  • Creating an item now takes you to it, instead of dropping you back on the full list.
  • Fixed: adding a category did nothing on a phone. It used a browser pop-up, which phone browsers block in an installed app, so it silently failed. It now asks inline - as does deleting a category.

This update adds a database column - reload the app once after updating.

1.87.0

You can now edit a stock entry after adding it. Made a typo in the quantity, entered the wrong price, or want to reword the note? Every hand-entered receive or scrap on an item's page now has an Edit button. Change what you need and save - the stock is recalculated, the material's average cost is re-derived, and the change is written to the activity log (what it was, what it became) so nothing happens silently. Entries that belong to something else - a purchase, a till sale, a production run, a transfer - still point you at the right place to fix them there.

  • Entries show everything you recorded, not just a quantity: how it was entered ("2 x 50 pcs" when you received boxes), the box price as well as the per-unit price, the date, and your note on its own line. An edited entry is marked as such.
  • Boxes are remembered properly. Receiving by the box used to stash "2 box" into the note as plain text and keep only the per-unit price, so the box price was gone for good. The pack details are now stored as real data - which is what lets the entry show the box price back to you, and lets you edit in boxes instead of converting in your head. The pack size is frozen as it was on the day.

This update adds database columns - reload the app once after updating.

1.86.1

Fix: long product names no longer break the Shop stock layout. On a phone, a long name (common on the online-shop products) overran the Local/Shop quantity columns and overlapped them. Names now wrap to at most two lines then trim with an ellipsis, and the SKU line trims too, so every row stays inside its column.

1.86.0

Sale locations now look like what they are. The locations screen is a set of tiles instead of a flat list: each carries a coloured kind accent and label - Counter, Pop-up, Market stall or Other - so a shop counter and a Saturday market no longer look identical. A status dot shows whether each can sell right now: green Ready to sell when active with stock, No stock when active but empty, Inactive when switched off.

  • Open till leads - the most-used screen is now the prominent action on the locations screen and on each location's page, not a faint toolbar link.
  • You can set a location's kind - the new-location and edit forms gained a Kind picker (Counter / Pop-up / Market stall / Other), the same kinds the till shows when you choose where to sell.

1.85.0

Refunds happen on the receipt itself now. A manager taps Refund items and the receipt's own line table gains a refund-quantity box on each still-refundable line - one table, read it and act on it, instead of the same items listed twice. Enter what's coming back, add an optional reason, Refund selected - or Void whole sale.

  • Voiding asks first, on the page - an inline confirmation with a clear warning, not a browser pop-up (which some devices silently swallowed). It only voids on the second, deliberate tap.
  • A voided sale now looks voided - a banner across the top, the receipt greyed, the total struck through.
  • Printing moved to its own bar above the receipt (Print 80mm / Print A4), instead of being tucked inside the header.

1.84.0

Sales now has a chart. The Sales screen gained a Sales over time graph above the receipts list - a bar per day of net takings (after refunds), so you can see the shape of trade at a glance instead of reading a table. It respects the location and date filters, calls out your best day, and for longer ranges it groups by week (over ~3 months) or month (over ~1.5 years) so the bars stay readable. Hover a bar for that day's takings and sale count. Days with no sales show as a gap; an empty range says so plainly.

1.83.0

The menu is now grouped. The navigation had grown to a flat list of nineteen entries; it is now organised into five labelled sections - Catalogue, Trade, Sell, Stock and Admin - with Help pinned at the bottom. The same grouping is used on the desktop sidebar and in the phone menu, and you only see the sections your access level can reach.

The phone bottom bar is now a steady five: Home, Products, Sell, Scan and Menu. Sell opens the till if you can take payments, or Shop stock otherwise; Menu opens the full grouped list. The bar no longer changes shape as you move around.

Nothing moved that you can't still reach, and no destination changed what it does - this is purely how the menu is arranged.

1.82.0

Viewer accounts no longer see money. The Viewer level was read-only but could still open orders, purchases, partner statements and reports — all full of costs, margins and what partners owe. A viewer's job is to see what is in stock and where, and that is now exactly what they get:

  • Hidden from viewers: costs, margins, B2B prices, purchase history and what a delivery cost — stripped from every item payload on the server, not just hidden on screen. Retail prices stay visible.
  • Off limits for viewers: Orders, Purchases, Stock notes, Partners, Out on consignment, Held stock, Produce and Reports — the API refuses (operator and up), and the menu no longer offers doors that would be refused.
  • Still theirs: Overview, Products, Materials, Shop stock, Scan and Help — quantities, locations, low-stock flags.
  • Operators, managers and administrators see everything they did before.

1.81.0

Security and robustness hardening following a full audit (nothing was found being exploited — these close doors before anyone knocks):

  • The app refuses to be embedded in other sites and tells the browser exactly where scripts and data may come from (security headers incl. a Content-Security-Policy on every app, till and sign-in page).
  • Sign-in attempts are throttled per account as well as per address — and the same limit now covers wp-login.php, which previously had none. Eight failures locks sign-in for 10 minutes.
  • Updates are checksum-verified. Each release publishes its fingerprint and the plugin refuses a package that doesn't match.
  • CSV exports are Excel-safe — values starting with = + - @ no longer open as live formulas (real negative numbers untouched).
  • Signing out on a shared device clears the app's offline copy.

Fix: a till left open overnight no longer dies silently. When the session expires the app now says so and one tap continues — instead of every tap failing with a cryptic error until someone reloads. Queued offline work is kept.

Faster: the Material prices screen loads in three queries instead of two per material. Housekeeping: the activity log keeps 12 months and prunes older entries daily.

1.80.0

New: Correction mode — undo entries made by mistake (Settings, Administrator). Turn it on and an Undo button appears beside every stock entry on an item's page. It covers the three things that had no way back: hand-entered stock (receive, scrap, set quantity), production runs, and stock pushed to or pulled from a sale location.

  • It shows you what will happen before it happens — every item that moves, its stock now and what it becomes. Undoing one leg of a production run undoes the whole run: every component goes back into stock and everything it made comes back out, all listed before you commit.
  • Nothing is erased. The original entry is kept and struck through, and an opposite entry cancels it — so the history still explains itself months later. Cancelled pairs are folded away behind a count so the list stays readable.
  • It won't let you undo the wrong thing. An entry that came from a purchase, a till sale, a consignment note or an order says so and points you at the right place — those already have their own undo. An entry can't be cancelled twice, and a cancellation can't itself be cancelled.
  • If undoing leaves stock below zero — because some of it has already been used or sold — it warns you and lets you proceed, since that is exactly how "I typed 100 instead of 10" gets fixed.
  • Only administrators can switch the mode on, and only for themselves, so a stray tap on a phone can't rewrite stock history. Every correction is recorded in the activity log with the reason you type.

1.78.0

1.77.1

1.77.0

See what materials cost — and choose what your recipes cost from.

  • On each material's page: “What it costs.” Two figures side by side — what the stock you're holding cost you, and what it costs to buy now — with the change between them flagged when prices have moved. sections.description: Companion plugin for VGC Stock Manager. Exposes a tiny, token-authenticated REST surface for reading and adjusting WooCommerce product stock quantities only (never orders or customers).
sections.changelog:
0.7.0

What the shop refunded, line by line. Every line now carries how many of it were refunded and how much money came back for it, and an incremental read also returns the orders whose refunds changed since the cursor — a refund does not always mark its order as modified. Read only, as before.

0.6.1

Fix: a refund in the shop could stop orders reaching the backoffice. WooCommerce can hand back a refund alongside the orders it lists. Treating it as an order was a fatal error, that page of the answer failed, and the backoffice’s pull stopped there — so every order after the refund stayed out of the books. Refunds are now asked to be left out, and skipped if they appear anyway.

0.6.0

Orders now say how they were paid, and what the gateway took for it. The gateway’s own recorded fee is passed on where it keeps one, so the backoffice can book what the transaction actually cost rather than an estimate. Reported as nothing at all — never as zero — when the gateway records none, so “nobody said” can be told from “it was free”.

The shop also lists the payment methods it offers, so a fee rule can be set against each by name.

Still read only, and still anonymous: a gateway’s name and a number it charged are not customer data, and no name, address, email or phone is ever transferred.

0.5.1

Fix: the API says it must not be cached. On a host with a page cache in front of it, the backoffice could be handed a cached answer to “what has changed?” — so it recorded a sale for an order that had since been deleted, and could not see a cancellation at all. Nothing errored; both sides were working perfectly on stale data. Every response now says plainly that it must not be kept.

0.5.0

The shop can be asked what it has sold. Two new read-only endpoints for the backoffice: one that lists orders — number, status, dates, money and lines, with each line marked as a product, postage or a fee — and one that lists the order statuses this shop actually uses, including any you have added yourself.

Read only, and anonymous. No name, address, email, phone or customer id ever leaves the shop, so no second copy of your customer list is created anywhere else. Nothing here can cancel, refund, complete or edit an order; the bridge still only reads.

Nothing changes on the shop until the backoffice is set up to pull. Installing this on its own is safe and has no visible effect.

0.4.0 /products gains category/type filters and a virtual flag; new /product-categories endpoint. 0.3.0 /products returns full-size image URL. 0.2.0 GET /products so the backoffice can pull shop products in as items. 0.1.0 Initial release: token auth, ping, read stock, adjust (delta), set (absolute).
